projects.name: Disaggregated Decoding on Heterogeneous GPU–Dataflow AI Accelerators
projects.description: Overview: Heterogeneous LLM inference that separates GPU prefill from dataflow-accelerator decoding for long-horizon agents. Implementation: Develop the GPU-to-CSL execution path, including request handoff and state transfer between prefill and decode. Results: Executed prefill on an 8-GPU NVIDIA H200 SXM system and autoregressive decoding on Cerebras WSE-3.

projects.name: Long-Context KV Cache Management for Large-Scale Computer-Use Agents
projects.description: Overview: KV-cache scheduling for multiple long-horizon computer-use agents sharing GPU memory. Implementation: Develop cache allocation and residency scheduling across agent sessions, focusing on context reuse and memory pressure. Results: Evaluated KV-cache scheduling with 50 concurrent long-horizon agents on 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

projects.name: Distributed RL Rollout Acceleration on a 256-GPU Compute Cluster
projects.description: Overview: Distributed RL rollout infrastructure targeting load balance, lower GPU idle time, and stable execution. Implementation: Built a Go task-scheduling layer using vLLM and speculative decoding to coordinate variable-length rollout tasks across the cluster. Results: Tested the rollout system at a scale of 256 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs at NERSC.

projects.name: BioWorkflow-Gym
projects.image_note: Unmodified screenshot of an agent-built Hi-C workflow in Galaxy's workflow editor; native 642 × 342 resolution retained.
projects.alt: Agent-built Galaxy workflow graph for Hi-C contact-map generation and assembly curation.
projects.description: Overview: A training and evaluation environment for long-horizon scientific agents constructing and executing verifiable bioinformatics workflows. Implementation: Built a Python/BioBlend system on NERSC using peer-reviewed Galaxy IWC workflows; ran 50 concurrent secure rollouts lasting 1.5–2 hours each. Results: Weight-free skill evolution improved the composite score from 33/100 to 51/100 (+54.5%), measuring workflow graph completion, execution completion, and result correctness.

projects.alt: CSL-LLM SDK architecture: model planning, handwritten CSL, compilation, runtime execution, and reference validation.
projects.description: Overview: LLM execution on programmable wafer-scale hardware, with explicit control over computation, communication, and persistent model state. Implementation: Implemented CSL kernels, Python host orchestration, and tensor placement on Cerebras CS-3 at Argonne National Lab AI Testbed. Results: The complete 64-layer Qwen3.8 network generated two continuous sentences plus EOS (37 tokens) on one physical WSE-3. Strict CPU numerical parity remains open.

projects.name: MIMD Dataflow / Pragma HLS
projects.image_type: Screenshot of the repository's exact Mermaid diagram
projects.image_note: Project design Mermaid diagram rendered locally with Mermaid 10.9.4 and captured via CUA because GitHub's Mermaid embed did not load. Diagram content and connections are unchanged.
projects.alt: Pragma HLS compiler pipeline from C++ tensor programs through spatial planning and generated CSL to numerical and protocol validation.
projects.description: Overview: A compiler and programming model for treating spatial dataflow architectures as general-purpose MIMD numerical accelerators. Implementation: Built a Python compiler with a C++ tensor frontend and CSL code generation for PE placement, communication routing, and buffer-lifetime management. Results: The published Cerebras SDK-simulator snapshot records 141 qualified configurations, including a 25-node resident attention graph, with numerical and communication-protocol validation.

projects.name: Fused Kernel on FPGA Using HLS
projects.description: Overview: Fused FPGA computation exposed as a custom instruction callable from software. Implementation: Used HLS to add dedicated buffers around fixed systolic-array IP and integrated the fused operation with an ARM C++ compiler. Results: Tested on Xilinx U280, exposing a fused hardware operation as one custom instruction callable through an ARM C++ compiler.

projects.name: Accelerated Radon Transformation on FPGA Using HLS
projects.description: Overview: A stream-processing unit for hardware-accelerated Radon-transform computation. Implementation: Used HLS and HDL to connect spatially arranged processing elements into a streaming hardware pipeline. Results: Built and tested a Radon-transform stream-processing unit on Xilinx Zynq-7010.
